data.title: Superseding a decision is one event, not two edits
data.why: In a file-based tool superseding means writing the new record and marking the old one. Sources are blunt that teams do the first and skip the second, which is how a reversed decision keeps looking authoritative. Here the new event carries supersedes and the backward link is derived while folding, so nobody writes the second half and nobody forgets it. A mutation test confirms the derivation is load-bearing.
data.rejected: A separate decision.superseded event — it would reintroduce the two-write problem inside our own model, since the second event can simply be missing.
